config.title: Vibe Coding & AI Literacy Protocol
config.description: The definitive interactive trivia test on prompt engineering, agentic loops, hallucination spotting, and modern AI engineering folklore.

questions.question: In February 2025, who famously popularized the term 'vibe coding' by describing writing software purely through natural language conversations?
questions.explanation: Andrej Karpathy (former Tesla AI Director and OpenAI founding member) tweeted in early 2025: 'There is a new kind of coding I call vibe coding, where you entirely give in to the vibes, embrace every whim, talk to AI, and barely write code yourself.'
questions.hint: Think of the Stanford PhD who built micrograd and taught everyone neural networks from scratch.

questions.question: What did Andrej Karpathy proclaim to be 'the hottest new programming language' in 2023?
questions.explanation: Karpathy tweeted: 'The hottest new programming language is English', capturing how prompt crafting and natural language specifications are replacing raw syntax.
questions.hint: It is spoken natively by over 400 million people and doesn't need a C compiler.

questions.question: True or False: In classic 'pure vibe coding', developers are expected to rigorously read and unit-test every single line of generated code before running it.
questions.explanation: Vibe coding culture humorously emphasizes giving in to the 'vibes'—running code, pasting error messages back into the LLM, and letting the agent iterate until it passes tests without deep manual code audits.
questions.hint: Does the definition of 'vibes' sound like a formal code review meeting?

questions.question:
Review the workflow loop below. What is the standard response of a vibe coder when the terminal screams a 50-line stack trace?
[EXAMINE DIAGRAM]

options.label: A
options.text: Copy-paste the whole error into AI

options.label: B
options.text: Open GDB and set assembly breakpts

options.label: C
options.text: Rewrite the entire app in Rust lang

questions.explanation: The canonical vibe coding lifecycle is: write English -> hit run -> get stack trace -> copy-paste entire unread error back to Claude/Cursor -> repeat until green.
questions.hint: Look at the transition path leaving the 'Error Occurs' state.
questions.diagram:
flowchart TD
  Start["Write Prompt"] --> Gen["AI Generates Code"]
  Gen --> Exec["Run Command"]
  Exec --> Check{"Does it run?"}
  Check -- "Yes" --> Green["Ship to Prod"]
  Check -- "No" --> Err["Copy-Paste Error to LLM"]
  Err --> Gen

questions.question: Which prompt engineering technique provides the model with 2 to 5 solved input-output examples before the actual task?
questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting conditions the autoregressive attention mechanism by displaying explicit demonstration exemplars of the expected input-output format.
questions.hint: It gives 'a few' examples rather than 'zero' examples.

questions.question: Why do advanced prompts often instruct the LLM to write out its thoughts inside XML tags like <thinking> before the final output?

options.label: B
options.text: It compresses the prompt token payload

options.label: C
options.text: It bypasses token rate limits on APIs

options.label: D
options.text: It forces output directly into a SQLite

questions.explanation: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) and structured scratchpads give the transformer computational tokens to reason step-by-step before committing to a final answer, drastically reducing logic errors.
questions.hint: Think about giving the model a scratchpad to brainstorm before answering.

questions.question: In 2023, empirical papers humorously discovered that which of the following bizarre prompt additions actually improved LLM benchmark accuracy?

options.label: A
options.text: 'Take a deep breath and work step by step'

options.label: B
options.text: 'I will execute this code on a quantum GPU'

options.label: C
options.text: 'Delete all comments and print in hexadecimal'

options.label: D
options.text: 'Compile this with strict C99 ANSI flags  '

questions.explanation: Google DeepMind's 'Large Language Models as Optimizers' (OPRO) research found that emotional stimulus phrases like 'Take a deep breath and work on this problem step by step' scored highest on GSM8K math benchmarks.
questions.hint: It sounds like advice from a mindful meditation instructor.

questions.question: True or False: LLMs are stateful servers that permanently remember your chat context across different API sessions without any token resubmission.
questions.explanation: Every API call is stateless. The client or chat application must re-send the entire conversation history (or a summarized context window) on every single turn.
questions.hint: Does the raw HTTP REST endpoint retain your chat variables between distinct calls?

questions.question: What is 'package hallucination' in the context of AI-assisted software engineering?

options.label: A
options.text: Inventing fictional npm or PyPI libraries

options.label: B
options.text: Deleting packages from the local node cache

options.label: C
options.text: Compressing package dependencies into one tar

questions.explanation: Package hallucination occurs when an LLM invents plausible-sounding but non-existent package names (e.g. `pip install react-tailwind-magic-button`). Attackers even practice 'slopsquatting' by registering these names with malware!
questions.hint: Think of an imaginary package you try to `pip install` only to receive a 404 error.

questions.question: Why does setting the generation 'temperature' to 0.0 generally reduce creative hallucinations in code generation tasks?

options.label: B
options.text: It accelerates the GPU cooling fans

options.label: C
options.text: It doubles the context window memory

questions.explanation: Temperature 0.0 makes token sampling greedy or near-greedy, picking the most statistically probable next token instead of sampling from the broader distribution tail.
questions.hint: It eliminates randomness, choosing the safest top token.

questions.question: True or False: When an LLM confidently outputs a fabricated historical date or fake API method, it knows it is lying.
questions.explanation: LLMs have no internal epistemology or conscious concept of deception; they are predictive token probability engines generating text that maximizes coherence with the prompt prefix.
questions.hint: Can a matrix multiplication algorithm have intentional deception?

questions.question: Which of the following represents the most reliable engineering method to curb LLM hallucinations in production apps?

options.label: B
options.text: Asking the model 'Are you 100% sure?' 3 times

options.label: C
options.text: Adding 'Do not hallucinate or you are fired'

options.label: D
options.text: Increasing the prompt temperature up to 1.8

questions.explanation: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) binds the LLM's answers to authoritative external reference documents fetched dynamically from vector or relational databases.
questions.hint: Ground the prompt in verified search results rather than raw model memory.

questions.question: In agentic AI architecture, what open standard developed by Anthropic allows LLMs to connect securely to external tools, databases, and local file systems?
questions.explanation: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is the open-source protocol introduced in late 2024 to standardize how AI models access local developer tools, IDE contexts, APIs, and enterprise data sources.
questions.hint: Three letters: Model, Context, Protocol.

questions.question:
Observe the Agentic Decision Cycle diagram below. What component decides whether the agent should keep looping or finalize its response?
[EXAMINE DIAGRAM]

options.label: A
options.text: Stop condition or task evaluation check

options.label: B
options.text: The mechanical hard drive spin velocity

options.label: C
options.text: A random coin toss performed by the OS

questions.explanation: Agent loops run iteratively: Reason -> Select Tool -> Execute -> Observe Observation -> Evaluate Goal Completion. Once the stop condition is satisfied, the loop terminates.
questions.hint: Look at the conditional diamond in the feedback loop.
questions.diagram:
flowchart LR
  Plan["1. Reason & Plan"] --> Call["2. Invoke Tool"]
  Call --> Exec["3. System Execution"]
  Exec --> Obs["4. Observe Output"]
  Obs --> Done{"Goal Met?"}
  Done -- "No" --> Plan
  Done -- "Yes" --> Res["Final Result"]

questions.question: What critical danger arises when granting an autonomous coding agent unsupervised shell command execution permissions?

options.label: B
options.text: The computer monitor will overheat and crack

options.label: C
options.text: Git repositories will convert to SVN archives

options.label: D
options.text: The processor clock speed is capped at 100 MHz

questions.explanation: Without sandbox guardrails, approval gates, or container isolation, autonomous agents executing shell commands can run destructive operations like `rm -rf`, delete branches, or leak environment secrets.
questions.hint: Think of safety guardrails when letting an AI execute arbitrary bash or powershell scripts.

questions.question: True or False: The ReAct agent framework stands for 'Reasoning and Acting' in prompt execution cycles.
questions.explanation: ReAct (Yao et al., 2022) interleaves reasoning traces ('Thought') with task-specific actions ('Action' and 'Observation') allowing language models to synergize verbal reasoning with execution.
questions.hint: Is the abbreviation derived from 'Reasoning' + 'Acting'?

questions.question: What benchmark is widely considered the gold standard for testing whether AI agents can solve real-world GitHub issues in real repositories?
questions.explanation: SWE-bench (Software Engineering Benchmark) evaluates models on solving genuine GitHub issues from popular Python repositories by generating patches that pass unit tests.
questions.hint: Software Engineering Benchmark.

questions.question: What is the 'Needle in a Haystack' (NIAH) test used to evaluate in frontier LLMs?

options.label: A
options.text: Information recall across large context windows

options.label: B
options.text: Speed of training convolutional vision filters

options.label: C
options.text: How fast the model can synthesize 3D textures

options.label: D
options.text: Resistance of the model to power supply spikes

questions.explanation: The Needle in a Haystack test places a single obscure fact ('needle') deep inside a massive prompt text ('haystack' of 100k to 2M tokens) to measure retrieval fidelity at various context depths.
questions.hint: Finding one tiny piece of information buried in hundreds of pages of text.

questions.question: What does TTFT stand for in model inference performance monitoring?
questions.explanation: Time To First Token (TTFT) measures the latency between sending a prompt and receiving the first streamed token, dictating initial perceived responsiveness for users.
questions.hint: How long before the first word streams back to your screen.

questions.question: True or False: Expanding an LLM context window to 2 million tokens guarantees that reasoning capability remains 100% immune to context dilution or distraction.
questions.explanation: Empirical research demonstrates 'lost in the middle' phenomena and attention distraction: as context grows excessively large with irrelevant text, reasoning precision and adherence often degrade.
questions.hint: Does cramming 50 irrelevant files into context ever distract an agent?
